clue.text: Girl protects source, hiding our origin

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so the girl's name wraps round the other piece

parts.note: Nancy is a girl's name

indicators.note: hiding here means the word our is tucked away, taken out of source and lost from view

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl shields a source while concealing where we come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origin' at the end looks like part of the surface's sentence, but it is the definition; 'hiding our' leaves SCE for 'protects' to wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascency is a rare word for birth or beginning, the coming into being of something.

clue.text: Solitary woman's task aboard a new ship

indicators.note: something aboard a ship is carried inside it, so one piece sits within the others

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a chore is a routine task

explanation.surface: A lone woman takes on a job on board a freshly built vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of woman's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'aboard' is the old convention of a piece set between the letters of SS.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchoress is a female religious recluse who lived walled up alone, hence a solitary woman.

clue.text: The Spanish stick about to set up supper room

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting up raises the pieces so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
a cane is a walking stick
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A Spaniard plans to raise a stick in an eating room.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'to set up', turns the whole run EL + CANE + C, giving CENACLE read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cenacle is the upper room where the Last Supper was held, so the word means a supper room.

clue.text: Nothing spoken of prisons

indicators.note: spoken of says the word is to be heard, so the entry sounds like it

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: No one talks about jails.
explanation.walkthrough: NICK is British slang for a prison or police station.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a nick is a jail or police station, so nicks are prisons.

clue.text: That old French city's origin is forgotten

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter, and forgetting it drops that letter

parts.note: Lyon is a city in France; the 's is the link 'is'

explanation.surface: A Gallic town no longer remembers where it came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origin is forgotten' removes the L from LYON.
explanation.definitionFit: Yon is an archaic demonstrative meaning that one over there, so it stands for that in old usage.

clue.text: No good getting stuck in pipe over swamp

indicators.note: a piece stuck in another is lodged inside it
over means turned over, so the pipe's word is read backwards

parts.note: a flue is a chimney pipe

explanation.surface: A useless thing has jammed in a pipe above a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swamp' reads as a noun in the surface but is the verb; 'over' gives EULF and 'getting stuck in' lodges the pair after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To engulf is to swamp or overwhelm, as a wave does a boat.

clue.text: Heroic helper turned up name of funeral ode

parts.note: epic means heroic

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reverses the word so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: an aide is a helper

explanation.surface: A brave assistant appears, named in a lament for the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses AIDE to EDIA. The definition is adjectival: 'of funeral ode', since the answer describes an elegy.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicedian is an adjective describing an epicedium, a funeral song or elegy.

clue.text: Shooting plan involved interrupting stay

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of something

parts.note: a guy is a rope used as a stay to hold a tent or mast

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A scheme for firing guns gets tangled and cuts short a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stay' looks like a visit but is a supporting rope; 'involved' scrambles to NPLA and 'interrupting' breaks into the rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunplay is the use of firearms, shooting.

clue.text: Linguists primarily are to preserve ancient tongue

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: an are is a unit of area, abbreviated A
to tin food is to preserve it in a can

explanation.surface: Language experts are mainly there to keep an old language alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is not a verb here but the metric unit of area, a hundred square metres, shortened to A.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is the classical language of ancient Rome.

clue.text: I vote against representative figure

parts.note: a con is a vote or argument against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Someone declares opposition to a symbolic image.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is an image or person that stands for something, a representative figure.

clue.text: US city reversing some Britannic niceties

indicators.note: reversing says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An American town turns away from British refinements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks ITANNICNIC out of the clue's words and 'reversing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cincinnati is a city in Ohio.

clue.text: Standard request for money by street person

parts.note: a touch is an attempt to borrow or cadge money
one means a person, as in 'one never knows'

explanation.surface: A beggar on the street asks for cash as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: To make a touch, or touch someone for money, is British slang for asking to borrow it.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchstone is a standard against which things are judged, from the stone used to test gold.

clue.text: Blood group broken down in achy inflammation of nails

parts.note: O is a blood group

indicators.note: broken down means wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A blood type collapses in an aching condition of the nails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is part of what 'broken down' scrambles, giving NYCHIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Onychia is the medical name for inflammation of the nail bed.

clue.text: Wild cat evacuated lonely New Cross

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, leaving only the outer letters of the word

parts.note: a cross is drawn as X

explanation.surface: A deserted lonely district of London is home to an animal on the loose.
explanation.walkthrough: New Cross is an area of south-east London, which the surface uses as a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild cat with tufted ears.

clue.text: Late money in bank

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a cent is a coin, a piece of money

explanation.surface: Money arrived late at the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is a verb, as in 'bank on', meaning rely.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means lately, not long ago, so it can stand for late as an adverb.

clue.text: Canvas flaps and fleet isn't moving

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The sails flap while the navy stays still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges FLEET ISNT to give the answer; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Tent flies are the canvas flaps covering a tent's door or forming its outer sheet.

clue.text: Pygmy losing head in the way of an antelope

indicators.note: losing its head drops the first letter of the word

parts.note: pygmy as an adjective means tiny
a la, from French, means in the manner or way of

explanation.surface: A small person loses his head in the path of a deer-like beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pygmy' is an adjective meaning small; 'losing head' leaves INY. A LA is French borrowed into English.
explanation.definitionFit: The inyala, or nyala, is a southern African antelope with spiral horns.

clue.text: Learning about good, clear specs

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the others

parts.note: lore is knowledge or learning
nett means clear of deductions, as clear profit

explanation.surface: Study results in fine, clear glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: NETT is the British spelling of net, as in net profit; 'about' wraps the old word for learning round both pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of spectacles held to the eyes by a handle, so specs.

clue.text: Bone matter from nose is out of place

indicators.note: out of place means displaced, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something from a nose is wrongly positioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' rearranges NOSE IS to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossein is the collagen-rich organic matrix of bone.

clue.text: Twist cap off Spanish vino with dark red colour

indicators.note: taking a cap off removes the top, which in a down clue is the first letter

parts.note: tent is an old name for a deep red Spanish wine, from tinto
wine is a dark red colour

explanation.surface: Unscrew the top from a bottle of Spanish red that has a deep colour.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is a rare word for a Spanish red wine; 'cap off' cuts its T to leave ENT. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine is to twist together or round something.

clue.text: Barrow craft on types of running water

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: H and C are the hot and cold taps
art means craft or skill

explanation.surface: A boat glides on streams of flowing water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a boat but means skill, ART; 'types of running water' are H AND C, hot and cold taps.
explanation.definitionFit: A handcart is a small cart pushed by hand, like a barrow.

clue.text: Deception keeps fitting one legend

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the trick surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a con is a deception or swindle
apt means fitting
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A trick retains a suitable myth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legend' suggests a myth, but it is the text printed under a picture; 'keeps' wraps the swindle round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is the caption or explanatory text under a picture or map.

clue.text: Piece capturing knight is a little bit of a nuisance

definitions.text: a little bit of a nuisance

indicators.note: capturing means taking in, so the knight goes inside

parts.note: a gat is slang for a gun, also called a piece
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: In chess, a piece taking a knight is slightly annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' suggests chess, but it is gun slang, GAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small biting fly, a tiny pest.

clue.text: A German upcoming eleven gets in the spirit

indicators.note: gets in means enters, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: ein is German for a
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, and a team of eleven

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming German football team gets into the right frame of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' gives NIE in a down entry; 'eleven' is the side in football or cricket that 'gets in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nixie is a water sprite of Germanic folklore, a spirit.

clue.text: Tropical shrub faring badly by short grass

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put wrongly together
short means cut short, losing a last letter

parts.note: panic is a grass, as in panic grass

explanation.surface: A tropical bush is doing poorly beside cut lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges FARING to FRANGI; 'short' cuts the C off PANIC. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Frangipani is a tropical shrub or tree with fragrant flowers.

clue.text: King George set about a certain hopeless case

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so King George surrounds the other piece

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
one means a certain, as in 'one day'

explanation.surface: A king begins a particular lost cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' looks like 'began', but signals the royal cipher wrapped around the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone or something beyond saving, a hopeless case.

clue.text: In the box I shuffled, taking in current show

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so one piece goes within the other
shuffled means mixed up like cards

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone shuffles things in a box while watching an exhibition of current affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuffled' rearranges INTHEBOXI, and 'taking in' adds the I for current inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibition is a public show of art or objects.

clue.text: Happens to keep northern people in office

indicators.note: to keep means to hold within, so the verb surrounds the other piece

parts.note: is means exists or occurs, as in 'there is'

explanation.surface: Something occurs to keep the northerners in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happens' gives IS in the sense of taking place or existing.
explanation.definitionFit: The ins are the party or people currently in office, as opposed to the outs.

clue.text: Curious about ignition regularly missing

indicators.note: regularly missing drops every other letter, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about a car's ignition repeatedly failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly missing' keeps the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of IGNITION.
explanation.definitionFit: To be into something is to be keen on or interested in it.

clue.text: Sol spinning around before Greek sea god

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the sun wraps the other piece
spinning means turning round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: Sol is the sun
ere means before

explanation.surface: The sun turns round ahead of a Greek god of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Sol is the Roman sun god, so the name gives its common noun; 'spinning' makes NUS and 'around' wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nereus was the old man of the sea in Greek myth, father of the Nereids.

clue.text: Reduced hour in daylight experience

indicators.note: in places the hour within the daylight

parts.note: sun means sunlight or daylight
ken means knowledge or range of experience

explanation.surface: An hour of daylight is cut short in one's experience.
explanation.walkthrough: KEN, as in 'beyond my ken', is one's range of knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrunken means made smaller, reduced in size.
